prompt: An angle of $200^\circ$ is drawn in standard position. In which quadrant does its terminal side land?
hint: The quadrants are marked off every $90^\circ$: I ends at $90^\circ$, II at $180^\circ$, III at $270^\circ$, IV at $360^\circ$.

hints.text: The quadrants are marked off every $90^\circ$: I ends at $90^\circ$, II at $180^\circ$, III at $270^\circ$, IV at $360^\circ$.
Yes — $180^\circ < 200^\circ < 270^\circ$, so the terminal side is in Quadrant III.

explanation: Starting from the positive $x$-axis and sweeping counterclockwise, you pass $90^\circ$, $180^\circ$, and $270^\circ$ as you cross into each new quadrant.
Since $200^\circ$ sits between $180^\circ$ and $270^\circ$, the terminal side is in the third quadrant.

alternativeExplanations.title: Walk it around
steps: Sweep $180^\circ$ first — that takes you to the negative $x$-axis, pointing left.
You still have $20^\circ$ to go, which tips the ray slightly downward from that leftward direction.
Left and down together is Quadrant III.
